A 50-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting chronic dyspnea and fatigue that has remained
stable over the past 3 months. Her medical history includes COPD and type 2 diabetes, with current
medications of albuterol, tiotropium, and metformin. She has a 50 pack-year smoking history and
currently smokes half a pack daily. Her vital signs show: | Temperature | 37.3°C (99°F) | | --- | --- | |
Blood pressure | 128/78 mm Hg | | Heart rate | 82/min | | Respiratory rate | 20/min | | Oxygen saturation
| 93% on room air | Physical examination reveals bilateral moderate inspiratory wheezing. Structural
examination shows limited thoracoabdominal diaphragm movement, asymmetrical motion of right ribs
7-10 compared to the left during inspiration, and bilateral sternal border tenderness on palpation.
Which muscle should be targeted for muscle energy treatment in this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Diaphragm (B) External intercostals (C) Anterior scalene (D) Quadratus lumborum (E)
Sternocleidomastoid (F) Serratus anterior (G) Latissimus dorsi (H) Scalene muscles (I) Rectus
abdominis (J) Pectoralis major
 A. Rectus abdominis
B. Sternocleidomastoid
C. External intercostals
D. Anterior scalene
E. Scalene muscles
F. Quadratus lumborum

G. Pectoralis major
H. Diaphragm
I. Serratus anterior
J. Latissimus dorsi
